subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>, Priya Singh <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Hi Raj / Priya —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and next steps. I summarized the technical bits below so your engineering team can validate — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Pain points (what Finly told us):
- User-facing streaming chat is perceived as sluggish. Current streaming UX shows delayed first-byte and long tail for final tokens.
- Backend: single-turn generation p95 for 512-token responses ~1.2s (on your current hosted model infra). Streaming requests see bigger variance, p95 approaching ~1.8–2.0s.
- Concurrency: expected steady state ~150 concurrent streaming sessions (active websockets) with peaks to ~300 during market opens.
- Throughput: peak QPS for short completions ~600 qps; longer streaming sessions reduce available concurrency.
- Cost: want to reduce per-token inference cost without regressing quality.

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
- p95 latency for interactive streaming <= 350ms for typical user flows (first token under 150ms, steady streaming p95 <=350ms).
- System supports 150 steady concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation up to 300 (fallback policies).
- End-to-end UX: consistent token-by-token streaming (no big pauses), < 10% error rate under load.

Current stack and constraints:
- Finly is running a mix of open models on a managed GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100-ish) behind a custom gateway.
- They have prefix caching for some prompt templates but no cross-request KV cache.
- Networking: all inference traffic routes through an internal gateway in us-west-2.

Initial hypotheses from our side:
- Prefix/KV caching + optimized batching could reduce p95 substantially for repeated templates.
- Streaming-specific optimizations (smaller first-token path, early kernel selection) will improve first-byte latency.
- Smart routing to a lower-capacity, lower-cost model for non-critical requests could cut per-token cost.

Proposed next steps (what we agreed):
1) Redwood to share a short MA (mutual action) plan with scope + suggested benchmarks + artifacts (attached).
2) Finly to share one redacted example streaming trace and a 1-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) for us to run a sizing/benchmark.
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule 60-min infra session with Finly eng (recommend Aditya + Camila from our infra team).
4) Pilot: Redwood will propose a pilot configuration (dedicated pool + streaming profile) and target metrics to validate.

Attachments: finly-redwood-ma-plan.pdf (MA plan + timeline), p95-benchmark-summary.xlsx (example metrics schema).

Open Qs we flagged:
- Are the 150 concurrent sessions long-lived (minutes) or short bursts (seconds)? This impacts batching strategy.
- Any regulatory constraints around logging or persistence for traces we should know about?

I’ll follow up with proposed times for the technical deep-dive. Thanks again for your time — excited to help improve the streaming UX.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

---

From: Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@finly.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is great, very clear. Quick clarifications: 

- The 150 concurrent sessions are typically long-lived (3–12 minutes) during user workflows (so they persist enough that batching won't always combine unrelated requests). We do see short bursts during market open that spike to ~300 for ~30s.
- We can provide a 1-hour anonymized trace and the gateway logs for May 12th (I’ll scrub PII).
- Regarding logs: we need to keep audit trails internally; sharing sampled traces is fine but we cannot share full payloads with any vendor.

One ask: can Aditya/Camila include a short checklist of the data artifacts you need for sizing (trace format, sample rates, any example scripts)? Priya and I will coordinate.

If it helps, we’re available Wed 19 May 10:00–12:00 PT for the deep-dive.

—Raj
Raj Patel
Head of Engineering, Finly
raj@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>, Priya Singh <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Thanks Raj — Wed 19 May 10:00 PT works for us.

Aditya / Camila — I’ve captured Finly’s note about long-lived sessions and the logging constraints. Can you prepare a short checklist for the artifacts we need (trace + sample gateway logs + representative prompt templates)? Aim for a single-page checklist we can send to Raj/Priya today.

Draft agenda for the 60-min deep-dive (please tweak):
- 10m introductions + architecture overview (Finly)
- 15m production traffic + trace review (Finly)
- 20m Redwood initial analysis and proposed config (Aditya/Camila)
- 10m pilot scope and next steps
- 5m Q&A / action items

I’ll attach the MA plan link in the calendar invite. Raj/Priya — expect a short checklist from Aditya/Camila within the hour.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Thanks — sending checklist below so you have it in writing. I kept it short so Finly can pull the artifacts quickly.

Checklist for sizing + benchmark (single page):
- 1-hour anonymized production trace (timestamps, request ids, token counts, streaming markers). Preferred: JSONL with one event per line.
- Gateway logs for the same 1-hour window (time, src/dst IPs redacted, request_id, response status, bytes).
- Representative prompt templates (5–10 templates) with token lengths and any system messages.
- Typical client concurrency profile (histogram or short CSV: concurrency bucket -> percent time).
- Current model config: model name, batch size, max tokens, hardware spec (GPU type, mem), any quantization used.
- Any SLOs beyond p95 (p50/p99 targets, error budget).

Privacy note: Redwood can sign an NDA / DPA; we’ll only use redacted traces for sizing and will not persist payloads in the pilot.

Proposed deliverables from Redwood pre-deep-dive:
- Estimated pilot config (node types, pool size, streaming profile)
- Expected p95 improvement % and cost delta (ballpark)
- Short runbook for pilot integration (how to route traffic, fallbacks)

Raj — if you can drop the example trace link (or upload to the Drive link Marissa shared), we’ll pre-run a sizing pass before Wed.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
snippet: Post-call discovery recap capturing p95 targets, streaming UX issues, concurrency requirements and next steps (MA plan, trace + logs, technical deep-dive scheduled).
